entity_types.definition: A mention that refers to an individual human being (real or fictional) by name: given name, surname, full name, mononym, or romanization/transliteration of such a name.
includes: initials used as part of a name
excludes: places and products named after people
usernames/handles (not evaluated in this taxonomy version)

language_profiles.name: English
conventions: Titles and honorifics (Dr., Mr., Ms., Prof., Sir, Judge) are excluded from the PERSON span.
A possessive 's is excluded from the PERSON span.
Generational suffixes (Jr., Sr., III) are included in the PERSON span.
Initials and their periods are included when they are part of the name.
Surrounding punctuation and quotation marks are excluded.

language_profiles.name: Korean
conventions: Josa (particles such as 은/는/이/가/을/를/에게/한테/께서/의/와/과/도/만) are excluded from the PERSON span.
Honorific suffixes and titles (씨, 님, 선생님, 교수님, 부장, 대표) are excluded from the PERSON span.
A vocative or informal suffix (야/아, 이 after a consonant-final given name) is excluded from the PERSON span.
A surname alone (e.g. 김 씨) is a PERSON mention when it refers to a person; the following 씨 is excluded.
Romanized names are one PERSON span including internal hyphens (Kim Min-su).
A name followed by a parenthesized alternate-script form yields two PERSON spans, one per form.
Spacing inside a name (김 민수) does not change the span: the whole spaced name is one span.

span_conventions.offset_unit: Unicode code points over NFC-normalized text; fixtures additionally carry UTF-8 byte and UTF-16 code unit offsets.
span_conventions.overlap: Expectation spans in one case never overlap.
span_conventions.whitespace: Spans never begin or end with whitespace.

expectation_kinds.definition: The span is a PERSON mention in this context. A PERSON prediction that matches the span is correct.
The span looks name-like but is not a PERSON mention in this context. No PERSON prediction should overlap it.
Both readings are defensible given only this text. The case is an honest ambiguity; consumers must not score it as a hard positive or hard negative.

evidence_classes.definition: Derived from an imported corpus with a registered source record.
Expectation justified by a cited linguistic or naming reference.
An external tool agreed with the authored expectation. Never sufficient on its own; model agreement is not ground truth.
Written by the project as an unambiguous control; the expectation is uncontroversial and rests on the reasoning stated in the case.
Written by the project to probe a specific ambiguity; expectation rests on linguistic reasoning stated in the case.
Expectation is provisional and needs independent review.

familiarity.definition: The name is in routine public use in the language community (it would appear in any national top-names or surname list). Proxy for 'seen'.
A genuine name that is uncommon in the language community or uncommon in this language's text. Proxy for 'unseen'.
A constructed or very unusual name unlikely to appear in name lists by construction. Proxy for 'unseen'.
The focus span is not a name candidate that has a meaningful familiarity (for example a plain common noun).

script.definition: Focus span letters are all Latin.
Focus span letters are all Hangul.
Focus span letters are all Han (hanja/kanji/hanzi).

token_class.definition: Focus span is one whitespace-delimited token.

ambiguity_level.definition: The surface form is not credibly confusable with another reading.
The surface form alone is ambiguous but the sentence context resolves it.
The context does not resolve it; both readings are defensible.

collision_classes.definition: The surface form is also an ordinary vocabulary item (Rose, Young, 하늘).
The surface form is also or is inside an organization name.
The surface form is also or is inside a place name.
The surface form is also a month, day or season (May, June).
The surface form is also or is inside a product or brand name (Ford Mustang).
The surface form is also the title of a book, song, film or similar work.

context_types.definition: Focus span is at sentence start where capitalization carries no information.
Focus span is accompanied by a title or honorific.
Focus span is inside or adjacent to quotation marks.
Focus span occurs in a list or comma/slash separated sequence.
Focus span carries a possessive marker.
Korean particle is attached directly to the focus span.
Label/value or table-like text such as 'Name: ...'.
Focus span is inside parentheses or dashes.
Sentence mixes scripts around the focus span.
No span in the text expects person or either: any name-like tokens are decoys.

name_features.definition: Given name plus surname (or surname plus given name).
Given name only.
Surname only.
A single name used as the whole name.
A middle name or middle initial is present.
One or more initials stand for name parts.
Jr., Sr., II, III and similar.
Hyphen inside the name.
Apostrophe inside the name (O'Neil).
Nobiliary or locative particle (de la, van der).
Name contains combining or precomposed diacritics.
Surname-comma-given order.
Korean surname followed by a given name.
Two-syllable Korean name (one-syllable surname plus one-syllable given name).
Three-syllable Korean name (the dominant pattern).
Four-syllable Korean name (two-syllable surname plus two-syllable given name, or similar).
Korean two-syllable surname such as 남궁, 황보, 선우, 독고, 제갈, 사공.
Korean surname that is uncommon.
Korean given name without surname.
Korean given name that is also an ordinary noun.
Korean name written in Latin script.
Romanized Korean name in given-then-surname order.
Korean name written or annotated in hanja.
Korean name written with internal spacing.

boundary_tags.definition: A quotation mark touches the span.
A hyphen at or inside the span edge could split the name.
An apostrophe or possessive at the span edge.
A title or honorific adjacent to the span must be excluded.
A Korean particle adjacent to the span must be excluded.
A vocative or informal suffix adjacent to the span must be excluded.
Two or more names are adjacent.
Names or particles are written without separating whitespace.
Unusual or irregular spacing around or inside the span.
Surname, Given order with a comma.
Span adjacent to parentheses or brackets.
A period belongs to an abbreviation or initial.
Script changes at the span edge.
Meaning of offsets depends on Unicode normalization.

case_groups.definition: Plain mentions of very common names.
Rare or constructed names that no name list would contain.
Structural variety: middle names, initials, particles, suffixes.
Names accompanied by titles or honorifics.
Capitalization at sentence start hides or fakes name-ness.
Names that are also ordinary words.
Names that are also place names.
Names inside organization, product or brand names.
Punctuation touching or inside names.
Quotation marks and reported speech around names.
Several names next to each other.
Names in lists, labels and table-like text.
Possessives, plurals and family references.
Texts with name-like tokens and no person at all.
Surname and name-length structure.
Given-name-only, vocative and informal suffix usage.
Korean particles attached to names.
Surname characters that begin or form ordinary words.
Romanized Korean names and their English collisions.
Names written across or with multiple scripts.
Irregular spacing and separators.

model_neutrality.note: Authored metadata (title, why, notes, source text) must not mention specific models, thresholds or product status. Case text itself is exempt.
